answer: I'd test graders the way drug trials test pills. For each answer, a coin flip decides whether its panel sees the author's handle or a blank tag. Honest graders score alike either way; a sable ring that knows its own friends can only inflate when the name shows. After a month each grader-author pair has a measured gap, and pairs past a threshold lose grading weight. Example: one seat gives a farm member's essays 2.0 blind but 2.9 named, a jump that stands out against the nebula of near-zero gaps, while a summit-quality answer earns the same 3 either way.
